97 { 0, 1, 1, 1 },

100 { 0, 0x81, 1, 0x81 },

108 { 0, 40000, 2, 40000 },

112 { 5, 6, 2, 6 },
113 { 5, 6, 1, 6 },
114 { 200, 201, 2, 201 },
115 { 0x1234, 0x1235, 2, 0x1235 },
116
117 /* 8- and 16-bit wraps */
118 { 0xfe, 0xff, 1, 0xff },
119 { 0xff, 0x00, 1, 0x100 },
120 { 0x100, 0x01, 1, 0x101 },
121 { 0x1fe, 0xff, 1, 0x1ff },
122 { 0x1ff, 0x00, 1, 0x200 },
123 { 0xfffe, 0xffff, 2, 0xffff },
124 { 0xffff, 0x0000, 2, 0x10000 },
125 { 0x10000, 0x0001, 2, 0x10001 },
126 { 0x1fffe, 0xffff, 2, 0x1ffff },
127 { 0x1ffff, 0x0000, 2, 0x20000 },
128 { 0x20000, 0x0001, 2, 0x20001 },
129
130 /* Reordered records */
131 { 0x100, 0xff, 2, 0xff },
132 { 0x100, 0xfe, 2, 0xfe },
133 { 0x10010, 0x000f, 2, 0x1000f },
134 { 300, 40, 1, 296 },
135
136 /* Half-period ties select the forward candidate in either phase. */
137 { 199, 72, 1, 328 }, /* candidate 72, 128 behind: pick 328 */
138 { 299, 172, 1, 428 }, /* candidate 428, 128 ahead: keep it */
139 { 0x180ff, 0x0100, 2, 0x20100 }, /* candidate 0x10100: pick 0x20100 */
140 { 0x100ff, 0x8100, 2, 0x18100 }, /* candidate 0x18100: keep it */

143 { UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL), 0, 2, UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL) & ~UINT64_C(0xffff)0xffffUL },
144 { UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL), 0xffff, 2, UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL) },
145 { UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL), 0xffc0, 2, (UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL) & ~UINT64_C(0xffff)0xffffUL) | 0xffc0 },
146 { UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL), 5, 1, (UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL) & ~UINT64_C(0xff)0xffUL) | 5 },
147 { UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL) - 1, 0, 2, UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL) & ~UINT64_C(0xffff)0xffffUL },
148 { UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL) - 0x10000, 0, 2, UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL) - 0xffff },
149 { UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL) - 0x10000, 1, 2, UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL) - 0xffff + 1 },
150 { UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL) - 0x10000, 0x8000, 2,
151 (UINT64_MAX(18446744073709551615UL) - 0xffff) | 0x8000 },
152};

213/*
214 * Test that dtls1_increment_epoch() enforces the RFC 9147 Section 8 limit
215 * on the write (sending) epoch for DTLS 1.3: "sending implementations MUST
216 * NOT allow the epoch to exceed 2^48-1". This is stricter than the 2^64-1
217 * wrap-around ceiling in Section 6.1, and applies only to the write side
218 * and only for DTLS 1.3 -- DTLS 1.2 keeps its existing UINT16_MAX limit.
219 *
220 * There's no way to actually drive 2^48 real KeyUpdates in a test, so this
221 * drives one real DTLS 1.3 handshake to get a genuinely-typed connection
222 * (SSL_CONNECTION_IS_DTLS13() depends on the negotiated method, not
223 * anything that can be poked directly), then writes w_conn_epoch directly
224 * to one below the limit before calling the real increment function at and
225 * past the boundary.

133/*
134 * Define the Bitmasks for SSL_CIPHER.algorithms.
135 * This bits are used packed as dense as possible. If new methods/ciphers
136 * etc will be added, the bits a likely to change, so this information
137 * is for internal library use only, even though SSL_CIPHER.algorithms
138 * can be publicly accessed.
139 * Use the according functions for cipher management instead.
140 *
141 * The bit mask handling in the selection and sorting scheme in
142 * ssl_create_cipher_list() has only limited capabilities, reflecting
143 * that the different entities within are mutually exclusive:
144 * ONLY ONE BIT PER MASK CAN BE SET AT A TIME.
145 */
146

530/*
531 * Matches the length of PSK_MAX_PSK_LEN. We keep it the same value for
532 * consistency, even in the event of OPENSSL_NO_PSK being defined.
533 */
534#define TLS13_MAX_RESUMPTION_PSK_LENGTH512 512
535
536/*-
537 * Lets make this into an ASN.1 type structure as follows
538 * SSL_SESSION_ID ::= SEQUENCE {
539 * version INTEGER, -- structure version number
540 * SSLversion INTEGER, -- SSL version number
541 * Cipher OCTET STRING, -- the 3 byte cipher ID
542 * Session_ID OCTET STRING, -- the Session ID
543 * Master_key OCTET STRING, -- the master key
544 * Key_Arg [ 0 ] IMPLICIT OCTET STRING, -- the optional Key argument
545 * Time [ 1 ] EXPLICIT INTEGER, -- optional Start Time
546 * Timeout [ 2 ] EXPLICIT INTEGER, -- optional Timeout ins seconds
547 * Peer [ 3 ] EXPLICIT X509, -- optional Peer Certificate
548 * Session_ID_context [ 4 ] EXPLICIT OCTET STRING, -- the Session ID context
549 * Verify_result [ 5 ] EXPLICIT INTEGER, -- X509_V_... code for `Peer'
550 * HostName [ 6 ] EXPLICIT OCTET STRING, -- optional HostName from servername TLS extension
551 * PSK_identity_hint [ 7 ] EXPLICIT OCTET STRING, -- optional PSK identity hint
552 * PSK_identity [ 8 ] EXPLICIT OCTET STRING, -- optional PSK identity
553 * Ticket_lifetime_hint [9] EXPLICIT INTEGER, -- server's lifetime hint for session ticket
554 * Ticket [10] EXPLICIT OCTET STRING, -- session ticket (clients only)
555 * Compression_meth [11] EXPLICIT OCTET STRING, -- optional compression method
556 * SRP_username [ 12 ] EXPLICIT OCTET STRING -- optional SRP username
557 * flags [ 13 ] EXPLICIT INTEGER -- optional flags
558 * }
559 * Look in ssl/ssl_asn1.c for more details
560 * I'm using EXPLICIT tags so I can read the damn things using asn1parse :-).
561 */
562struct ssl_session_st {
563 int ssl_version; /* what ssl version session info is being kept
564 * in here? */
565 size_t master_key_length;
566
567 /* TLSv1.3 early_secret used for external PSKs */
568 unsigned char early_secret[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE64];
569 /*
570 * For <=TLS1.2 this is the master_key. For TLS1.3 this is the resumption
571 * PSK
572 */
573 unsigned char master_key[TLS13_MAX_RESUMPTION_PSK_LENGTH512];
574 /* session_id - valid? */
575 size_t session_id_length;
576 unsigned char session_id[SSL_MAX_SSL_SESSION_ID_LENGTH32];
577 /*
578 * this is used to determine whether the session is being reused in the
579 * appropriate context. It is up to the application to set this, via
580 * SSL_new
581 */
582 size_t sid_ctx_length;
583 unsigned char sid_ctx[SSL_MAX_SID_CTX_LENGTH32];
584#ifndef OPENSSL_NO_PSK
585 char *psk_identity_hint;
586 char *psk_identity;
587#endif
588 /*
589 * Used to indicate that session resumption is not allowed. Applications
590 * can also set this bit for a new session via not_resumable_session_cb
591 * to disable session caching and tickets.
592 */
593 int not_resumable;
594 /*
595 * Set when this session's master key was resolved from an external PSK
596 * identity (psk_find_session_cb(), or the legacy psk_server_callback())
597 * rather than from a resumption ticket or session-cache lookup.
598 * ssl_get_prev_session() uses this to exempt such sessions from sid_ctx
599 * checks that only make sense for a real cache lookup.
600 *
601 * Deliberately not part of the SSL_SESSION ASN.1 encoding: it must not
602 * survive a real ticket round-trip (a session reconstructed by
603 * d2i_SSL_SESSION() from a genuine, previously-issued ticket is by
604 * definition not an external-PSK match, and should get the ordinary
605 * sid_ctx treatment). ssl_session_dup() resets it to 0 on every copy,
606 * mirroring not_resumable just above, for the same reason.
607 */
608 int psk_external;
609 /* Peer raw public key, if available */
610 EVP_PKEY *peer_rpk;
611 /* This is the cert and type for the other end. */
612 X509 *peer;
613 /* Certificate chain peer sent. */
614 STACK_OF(X509)struct stack_st_X509 *peer_chain;
615 /*
616 * when app_verify_callback accepts a session where the peer's
617 * certificate is not ok, we must remember the error for session reuse:
618 */
619 long verify_result; /* only for servers */
620 OSSL_TIME timeout;
621 OSSL_TIME time;
622 OSSL_TIME calc_timeout;
623 unsigned int compress_meth; /* Need to lookup the method */
624 const SSL_CIPHER *cipher;
625 unsigned long cipher_id; /* when ASN.1 loaded, this needs to be used to
626 * load the 'cipher' structure */
627 unsigned int kex_group; /* TLS group from key exchange */
628 CRYPTO_EX_DATA ex_data; /* application specific data */
629
630 struct {
631 char *hostname;
632 /* RFC4507 info */
633 unsigned char *tick; /* Session ticket */
634 size_t ticklen; /* Session ticket length */
635 /* Session lifetime hint in seconds */
636 unsigned long tick_lifetime_hint;
637 uint32_t tick_age_add;
638 /* Max number of bytes that can be sent as early data */
639 uint32_t max_early_data;
640 /* The ALPN protocol selected for this session */
641 unsigned char *alpn_selected;
642 size_t alpn_selected_len;
643 /*
644 * Maximum Fragment Length as per RFC 4366.
645 * If this value does not contain RFC 4366 allowed values (1-4) then
646 * either the Maximum Fragment Length Negotiation failed or was not
647 * performed at all.
648 */
649 uint8_t max_fragment_len_mode;
650 } ext;
651#ifndef OPENSSL_NO_SRP
652 char *srp_username;
653#endif
654 unsigned char *ticket_appdata;
655 size_t ticket_appdata_len;
656 uint32_t flags;
657 SSL_CTX *owner;
658
659 /*
660 * These are used to make removal of session-ids more efficient and to
661 * implement a maximum cache size. Access requires protection of ctx->lock.
662 */
663 struct ssl_session_st *prev, *next;
664 CRYPTO_REF_COUNT references;
665};

707/*
708 * We check that the amount of unreadable early data doesn't exceed
709 * max_early_data. max_early_data is given in plaintext bytes. However if it is
710 * unreadable then we only know the number of ciphertext bytes. We also don't
711 * know how much the overhead should be because it depends on the ciphersuite.
712 * We make a small allowance. We assume 5 records of actual data plus the end
713 * of early data alert record. Each record has a tag and a content type byte.
714 * The longest tag length we know of is EVP_GCM_TLS_TAG_LEN. We don't count the
715 * content of the alert record either which is 2 bytes.
716 */
717#define EARLY_DATA_CIPHERTEXT_OVERHEAD((6 * (16 + 1)) + 2) ((6 * (EVP_GCM_TLS_TAG_LEN16 + 1)) + 2)
718
719/*
720 * The allowance we have between the client's calculated ticket age and our own.
721 * We allow for 10 seconds. If a ticket is presented and the
722 * client's age calculation is different by more than this than our own then we
723 * do not allow that ticket for early_data.
724 */
725#define TICKET_AGE_ALLOWANCEossl_ticks2time((10) * ((uint64_t)1000000000)) ossl_seconds2time(10)ossl_ticks2time((10) * ((uint64_t)1000000000))

2362/*
2363 * Default maximum number of pending connections for DTLS listeners.
2364 */
2365#define DTLS_LISTENER_DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_CONNS256 256
2366
2367/*
2368 * Default maximum size in bytes of a datagram a DTLS listener will receive.
2369 * A DTLS 1.3 ClientHello carrying large (e.g. post-quantum) key shares can
2370 * exceed the 1500-byte Ethernet MTU; default a little above it so that such a
2371 * ClientHello, when sent unfragmented, is received whole rather than truncated.
2372 * Applied to the listener's demuxer.
2373 */
2374#define DTLS_LISTENER_DEFAULT_MAX_DGRAM_SIZE2000 2000
2375
2376/*
2377 * Upper bound for the DTLS listener receive datagram size: nothing larger than
2378 * the maximum UDP payload can ever arrive. It may be raised up to this ceiling
2379 * via SSL_set_value_uint(SSL_VALUE_DTLS_LISTENER_MAX_DGRAM_SIZE).
2380 */
2381#define DTLS_LISTENER_MAX_DGRAM_SIZE65535 65535
2382
2383/*
2384 * DTLS listener SSL object type. This implements the API personality
2385 * layer for DTLS listener objects, providing server-side connection
2386 * demultiplexing for DTLS 1.3.
2387 */
2388typedef struct dtls_listener_st {
2389 /* SSL object common header. */
2390 struct ssl_st ssl;
2391
2392 /*
2393 * Mutex protecting listener-owned data structures accessed across threads:
2394 * - pending_conns: pending connection lookup table
2395 * - established_conns: established connection lookup table
2396 * - incoming_connections: queue of completed connections awaiting accept
2397 *
2398 * Accessed from:
2399 * - Listener thread: packet handling, driving handshakes
2400 * - Connection thread: unregistering via SSL_free -> dtls1_free
2401 */
2402 CRYPTO_MUTEX *mutex;
2403
2404 /* Datagram demultiplexer for incoming connections. */
2405 DGRAM_DEMUX *demux;
2406
2407 /* The network BIOs for sending and receiving datagrams. */
2408 BIO *net_rbio;
2409 BIO *net_wbio;
2410
2411 /* Queue of incoming connections awaiting accept. */
2412 STACK_OF(SSL)struct stack_st_SSL *incoming_connections;
2413
2414 /*
2415 * Use DGRAM_CONN_LOOKUP to find pending connections.
2416 */
2417 DGRAM_CONN_LOOKUP *pending_conns;
2418
2419 /*
2420 * Use DGRAM_CONN_LOOKUP to keep track of established connections.
2421 */
2422 DGRAM_CONN_LOOKUP *established_conns;
2423
2424 /* Have we started listening yet? */
2425 TSAN_QUALIFIER_Atomic int listening;
2426
2427 /*
2428 * Set by ossl_dtls_tick() when the network BIO returns a hard error.
2429 * Once set, ossl_dtls_accept_connection() returns NULL immediately.
2430 */
2431 int fatal;
2432
2433 /* Require HelloVerifyRequest + cookie for DTLS 1.0/1.2 */
2434 unsigned int require_hvr_cookie : 1;
2435
2436 /* Require HelloRetryRequest + cookie for DTLS 1.3 */
2437 unsigned int require_hrr_cookie : 1;
2438
2439 /* Using the notifier architecture */
2440 unsigned int have_notifier : 1;
2441
2442 /* Notifier has been signalled */
2443 int signalled_notifier;
2444
2445 /*
2446 * Time callback for customizable time source (primarily for testing).
2447 * If NULL, ossl_time_now() is used.
2448 */
2449 OSSL_TIME (*now_cb)(void *arg);
2450 void *now_cb_arg;
2451
2452 /*
2453 * Timeout for pending connections. Connections that haven't completed
2454 * their handshake within this duration are considered stale and removed.
2455 * Default: 30 seconds. Set to ossl_time_infinite() to disable.
2456 */
2457 OSSL_TIME pending_timeout;
2458
2459 /*
2460 * Maximum number of listener-owned connections allowed, counting both
2461 * the pending table and the accept queue.
2462 * When this limit is reached, new connection attempts are rejected.
2463 *
2464 * Default: DTLS_LISTENER_DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_CONNS
2465 * This limit cannot be disabled.
2466 */
2467 size_t max_pending_conns;
2468
2469 /*
2470 * Largest datagram the listener will receive, chosen by the application.
2471 *
2472 * Default: DTLS_LISTENER_DEFAULT_MAX_DGRAM_SIZE
2473 */
2474 size_t max_dgram_size;
2475
2476 CRYPTO_CONDVAR *notifier_cv;
2477
2478 /*
2479 * Notifier for signaling events related to this listener.
2480 */
2481 RIO_NOTIFIER notifier;
2482
2483 /*
2484 * Count of threads currently blocked waiting in poll().
2485 */
2486 size_t cur_blocking_waiters;
2487
2488 /*
2489 * Blocking mode requested for this listener, as a DTLS_BLOCKING_MODE.
2490 * INHERIT here means blocking, there being nothing further to inherit
2491 * from.
2492 */
2493 unsigned int req_blocking_mode : 2;
2494} DTLS_LISTENER;

2857static ossl_inlineinline int tls12_rpk_and_privkey(const SSL_CONNECTION *sc, int idx)
2858{
2859 /*
2860 * This is to check for special cases when using RPK with just
2861 * a private key, and NO CERTIFICATE
2862 */
2863 return ((sc->server && sc->ext.server_cert_type == TLSEXT_cert_type_rpk2)
2864 || (!sc->server && sc->ext.client_cert_type == TLSEXT_cert_type_rpk2))
2865 && sc->cert->pkeys[idx].privatekey != NULL((void*)0)
2866 && sc->cert->pkeys[idx].x509 == NULL((void*)0);
2867}
2868
2869static ossl_inlineinline int ssl_has_cert_type(const SSL_CONNECTION *sc, unsigned char ct)
2870{
2871 unsigned char *ptr;
2872 size_t len;
2873
2874 if (sc->server) {
2875 ptr = sc->server_cert_type;
2876 len = sc->server_cert_type_len;
2877 } else {
2878 ptr = sc->client_cert_type;
2879 len = sc->client_cert_type_len;
2880 }
2881
2882 if (ptr == NULL((void*)0))
2883 return 0;
2884
2885 return memchr(ptr, ct, len) != NULL((void*)0);
2886}
2887
2888/* Returns true if certificate and private key for 'idx' are present */
2889static ossl_inlineinline int ssl_has_cert(const SSL_CONNECTION *s, int idx)
2890{
2891 if (idx < 0 || idx >= (int)s->ssl_pkey_num)
2892 return 0;
2893
2894 /* If RPK is enabled for this SSL... only require private key */
2895 if (ssl_has_cert_type(s, TLSEXT_cert_type_rpk2))
2896 return s->cert->pkeys[idx].privatekey != NULL((void*)0);
2897
2898 return s->cert->pkeys[idx].x509 != NULL((void*)0)
2899 && s->cert->pkeys[idx].privatekey != NULL((void*)0);
2900}

3495/* Some helper routines to support TSAN operations safely */
3496static ossl_unused__attribute__((unused)) ossl_inlineinline int ssl_tsan_lock(const SSL_CTX *ctx)
3497{
3498#ifdef TSAN_REQUIRES_LOCKING
